title: Augmentations and faces of a hypercover retain its covering property
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits. Let $P$ be a class of morphisms containing all isomorphisms and stable under composition and base change. An augmented simplicial object $U_\bullet\to X$ is a $P$-hypercover if $U_0\to X$ and all matching maps $U_{n+1}\to(\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nU)_{n+1}$ lie in $P$; here the matching object is the finite limit over the proper faces, and the first matching object is $U_0\times_XU_0$. Then every augmentation component $U_n\to X$ and every face $d_i:U_n\to U_{n-1}$ lies in $P$. Consequently the map $U_n\to U_m$ attached to any injective order-preserving map $[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ lies in $P$. In particular, for algebraic spaces over a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-pc-scheme], if all matching maps are flat, locally finitely presented and surjective, then all augmentation components and face maps have these properties. Here flat and locally finitely presented mean those properties on etale scheme charts. For each such flat map $h:U_n\to U_m$ of algebraic spaces, the associated morphism of ringed small etale topoi is flat: $\mathcal O_{U_n}$ is flat over $h^{-1}\mathcal O_{U_m}$, so module pullback $h^*=\mathcal O_{U_n}\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O_{U_m}}h^{-1}(-)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exact; the same holds for every $U_n\to X$. No assertion of flatness of the degeneracy maps is made.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal C/X$. It has finite limits: its terminal object is $X\to X$, products are fibre products over $X$, and equalizers are pullbacks of diagonals. For a simplicial set $A$ with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, finite and nonempty in each degree, define $H(A)$ by the universal compatible family $(u_a:H(A)\to U_k)_{a\in A_k}$ over $X$, satisfying $U(\varphi)u_a=u_{A(\varphi)a}$. This object exists: apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-index-finite-initial] to the diagram $(k,a)\mapsto U_k$ in $\mathcal C/X$. Its full simplex-index limit is the limit over the finite initial truncation, which exists by [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. For $A=\varnothing$ set $H(A)=X$. A simplicial map $A\to B$ induces $H(B)\to H(A)$ by restriction of universal families, and these maps respect identities and composition by uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 017K (lemma-exists-hom-0-from-simplicial-set-finite), representing compatible families; the family formulation removes the unused coproduct hypothesis.

proof.text: Write $\Delta[r]_k=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([k],[r])$ and let $\partial\Delta[r]$ consist of the nonsurjective maps. A compatible family on $\Delta[r]$ is uniquely determined by its value at the identity: $u_\alpha=U(\alpha)u_{\mathrm{id}}$. Thus $H(\Delta[r])=U_r$. Every nonsurjective $\alpha$ factors uniquely as a surjection followed by an injective proper face; extending a proper-face family by $u_{\delta\sigma}=U(\sigma)u_\delta$ identifies boundary families with compatible proper-face families. Compatibility follows by factoring the composite of a proper-face injection with the next order map through its image and applying functoriality of $U$. Hence $H(\partial\Delta[r])=M_r(U)$, the matching limit over proper faces in $\mathcal C/X$; [lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces] identifies its canonical map with the matching morphism. For $r=0$ this reads $H(\varnothing)=X$ and $U_0\to X$. Isomorphism choices do not affect membership in $P$, since $P$ contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition.

source.place: Tags 0177 (lemma-simplex-map), 018V (lemma-cosk-shriek); direct universal-family verification in the slice.

proof.text:
Suppose $A\subset B$ adds a single nondegenerate $r$-simplex $b$ in the precise sense of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex]. That statement gives $B=A\amalg_{\partial\Delta[r]}\Delta[r]$. For every test object $T\to X$, giving a compatible family on $B$ is exactly giving families on $A$ and $\Delta[r]$ agreeing on the boundary: apply the stated pushout property to the simplicial set $k\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C/X}(T,U_k)$. Consequently the representing objects of step 1 form the pullback square
$$H(B)=H(A)\times_{M_r(U)}U_r.$$
The map $H(A)\to M_r(U)$ is restriction along the attaching boundary of $b$. Thus $H(B)\to H(A)$ is a base change of the matching map $U_r\to M_r(U)$, including $r=0$ when the base is $X$. By the hypercover assumption and base-change stability it belongs to $P$. This uses only finite limits, not coproducts in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), proof; the Hom pushout calculation of simplicial.tex Tag 017N is verified by universal families.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$, regard each face $\Delta[n-1]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$ as a simplicial subset. Both simplicial sets are finite and nonempty in every degree and have finitely many nondegenerate simplices: their nondegenerate simplices are exactly the injective maps into $[n-1]$ or $[n]$, respectively. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-add-simplices] to obtain a finite chain $A=W^0\subset\cdots\subset W^r=B$, starting at this face and ending at $\Delta[n]$, each inclusion satisfying step 3. Every intermediate $W^j$ contains the nonempty starting face and is a subset of $\Delta[n]$, so the finiteness/nonemptiness hypotheses of step 1 hold. By induction on $j$, $H(W^j)\to H(W^0)$ belongs to $P$: the base is an identity, and the induction step composes a map supplied by step 3 with the induction hypothesis. At $j=r$ this is the restriction $U_n\to U_{n-1}$, which step 2 identifies with the chosen face map. Thus all faces belong to $P$.

The zero augmentation $U_0\to X$ is in $P$ by hypothesis. Inductively, $U_n\to X$ is a face $U_n\to U_{n-1}$ followed by the augmentation $U_{n-1}\to X$, hence is in $P$ by step 4 and composition stability. An injective order map $[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ factors into the elementary injections omitting its missing vertices, successively removing one missing vertex. The associated simplicial operator is the reverse composite of those face maps; it belongs to $P$. If $m=n$ the map is the identity, which is also in $P$.

source.place: Tag 0DER (remark-P-covering), augmentation and face conclusions; injective-map clause by composition.

proof.text: For algebraic spaces over $S$, the fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] give finite limits in the slice over $X$: terminal $X$, products over $X$, equalizers by pulling back diagonals. Let $P$ be the conjunction flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. The chartwise stability statement [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], specialized to algebraic spaces, gives stability under composition and base change. Isomorphisms have all three properties: on charts they are etale, hence smooth, hence flat and locally finitely presented by that same statement; they are surjective since every target point has its inverse image. Apply steps 1–5 to this $P$. The assumed degree-zero covering and higher matching maps give all face maps, all augmentations and all injective simplicial operators flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. No degeneracy map was used.

source.place: Tag 0DER (remark-P-covering); spaces-simplicial.tex Tag 0DHF (lemma-coh-descent-qcoh-unbounded-for-fppf-hypercovering), flatness of augmentation components.

proof.text: For any one of these maps $h:Z\to W$ (a face, an injective simplicial operator or an augmentation), its chartwise flatness from step 6 implies, by [lem-sfb-space-flat-etale-ringed-comparison], that $\mathcal O_Z$ is flat over $h^{-1}\mathcal O_W$ on the small etale topos. This is exactly flatness of the associated morphism of ringed topoi. The comparison applies to arbitrary algebraic spaces over $S$ and imposes no separatedness, finite type or Noetherian hypothesis, so it applies to every term of this hypercover.

source.place: Tag 073C (lemma-flat-morphism-sites), applied to the maps obtained in step 6.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], $h^{-1}$ on modules with scalars transported to $h^{-1}\mathcal O_W$ is exact. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], flatness in step 7 means that tensoring over $h^{-1}\mathcal O_W$ with $\mathcal O_Z$ is exact. Their composite is the module pullback $h^*M=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O_W}h^{-1}M$ of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; thus it is exact. The same argument applies to augmentations. This proves precisely the asserted face and augmentation properties, without a claim about degeneracy maps.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), proof: exact inverse image followed by exact scalar extension.
